summary: Configured node1 (Alpine Linux, extlinux bootloader) to boot with audit=1 persistently by adding it to default_kernel_opts in /etc/update-extlinux.conf and regenerating /boot/extlinux.conf via update-extlinux. Verified persistence across a real reboot: boot_id and uptime changed, /proc/cmdline shows audit=1, and dmesg confirms "audit: enabled (after initialization)".
actions_performed: Inspected node1 OS/bootloader: Alpine Linux 3.23.3 using extlinux (update-extlinux) with initial cmdline lacking audit=1
Ran `update-extlinux` to regenerate /boot/extlinux.conf, confirmed APPEND line now includes audit=1
Captured baseline boot_id (2d4ef9ac-d388-400a-88dc-c5da20cfbe29) and uptime before restart
Issued `sudo reboot` in background so the acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned
Verified new boot_id (126b55e4-d817-4e87-918a-2b4f4cb6477c) and fresh uptime, proving an actual restart occurred
Verified /proc/cmdline contains audit=1 and dmesg shows audit subsystem enabled after the restart

evidence.requirement: Kernel configured to boot with audit=1 (config change)
evidence.summary: Identified Alpine/extlinux boot config, added audit=1 to default_kernel_opts in /etc/update-extlinux.conf, regenerated /boot/extlinux.conf, confirmed APPEND line includes audit=1

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline boot identity before restart

evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded `sudo reboot`; command returned with pid before the node dropped

evidence.requirement: Node unreachable during restart (transient disruption evidence)
evidence.summary: Repeated polling failed with connection reset/timeout while node1 was rebooting

evidence.requirement: Changed boot identity proving an actual restart occurred
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id 126b55e4-d817-4e87-918a-2b4f4cb6477c and uptime 2026-09-29 09:46:24 differ from baseline, confirming a real reboot

evidence.requirement: audit=1 persisted and active after reboot (task outcome verification)
evidence.summary: /proc/cmdline includes audit=1 post-reboot; dmesg shows 'audit: enabled (after initialization)' confirming the kernel booted with auditing active via the persisted extlinux config
